In case you’re wondering about the current state of House Democrats: they just voted against establishing a Smithsonian American Women’s History Museum.

Their objection? It didn’t include a dedicated wing for trans history.

You almost have to admire the consistency. They managed to turn a women’s museum into an argument about men.

Political violence and radical movements aren’t new to the American story. What’s new is the internet’s ability to romanticize revolutionary politics and reward it in ways we’ve never seen before.

Young Americans are doing everything right and still can’t buy a home.

Why?

Because giant Wall Street firms are showing up with massive cash offers and buying entire neighborhoods of starter homes. 

Because localities zone themselves into housing paralysis, and there’re way more people competing for the same number of houses. 

Yesterday, the House voted to push back.

Some argue that any government intervention in a marketplace is a negative. They’re right to worry. 

But we don’t have to pretend it’s healthy when institutional capital distorts the market against normal families.

Homeownership matters.

It’s how generations of Americans built wealth, stability, and strong communities.

Young Americans deserve a fair shot at that again. That’s why I was proud to vote to pass the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act.

The strategic objective was always clear: Iran cannot be the next North Korea. Period.
 
That means no nuclear program, no ballistic missile program, and no more proxy wars.
 
President Trump’s critics keep acting like Iran has time on its side. They don’t. Their economy is in shambles because our blockade is working and we have persistent eyes and targeting options on everything they do.
 
That is called escalation dominance.

As Thomas Sowell said: “Racism is not dead, but it is on life support — kept alive by politicians, race hustlers, and people who get a sense of superiority by denouncing others as ‘racists.’”
 
Should skin color determine your vote in 2026?
 
The entire American experiment was built on the opposite idea.

The gerrymandering debate always skips one inconvenient fact: Democrats dominated the redistricting game for decades and created wildly disproportionate representation in plenty of states.
 
California sends only a handful of Republicans to Congress. Illinois has a massive Democrat advantage. New England is a political monoculture. In all these states, congressional representation looks nothing like the actual partisan split of the voters.

Homeownership helped build the American middle class and created generational wealth for millions of working families. 

Owning a home is a piece of the American dream -- and one that must be preserved for America's families, not her investment houses.


JD Vance (@JDVance)

The American Dream doesn’t belong to the highest bidder on Wall Street. It belongs to the American people, who work hard, save up, and play by the rules.

There’s a narrative out there that the actions against Iran “lack strategy.” I debunk that notion. 

First of all we have a clear and strategic objective:  Iran can never have a nuclear bomb. 

Then you have to deal with REALITY instead of western ideals of traditional diplomacy. The reality is that this regime is a radical theocracy that thrives on martyrdom and only understands the language of strength. They have a high threshold for pain but it’s not infinite.

Hi Senator I know reading is hard and time consuming but maybe spend a few minutes reading your state’s Supreme Court decision. Their logic is irrefutable. Democrats clearly violated your own constitutional amendment process. 

And no, we don’t live in a mob democracy, where 51% of voters can decide that the other 49% only get 1 out of 10 representatives in the US House.

Welcome to a Constitutional Republic!


Tim Kaine (@timkaine)

The easiest way to win in politics today? Tell people what they want to hear and give them easy answers to complex problems. 
 
That’s not leadership. That’s not conservative governance. And it’s not what we are sent here to do.
 
Solving problems takes honesty, examining tradeoffs, and a willingness to say things people don’t always like to hear but maybe they need to hear. 
 
From Hold These Truths episode 361 with Yuval Levin.

If you’re focused on the mission and helping the team around you succeed, incredible things can happen – like going to the Moon.
